solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make-up container knight opens suddenly (4-4)

indicators.note: the knight gets inside the container, opening it up

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

annotation.surface: A cosmetics case is abruptly flipped open by a knight in armour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Make-up container" reads as one thing, a vanity case; split it into SLAP and BAG. N stands for knight because K is already the king.
annotation.definitionFit: Slap-bang means suddenly and violently, as in running slap-bang into someone.

clue.text: Stableboy on drug and getting loaded (5)

blocks.note: a lad is a stable hand at a racing yard

annotation.surface: A stable hand takes drugs and gets drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: "Loaded" hints at drink or money; here it just means carrying a load. "On" in a down clue puts LAD above what follows.
annotation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded down with a burden.

clue.text: Death is temporary (7)

definitions.note: Death is a noun and temporary an adjective; passing can be both

blocks.note: a gentle word for someone's death
short-lived, like a fancy that soon fades

annotation.surface: A grim observation that death is only a phase.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a philosophical claim; it is two separate meanings of one word joined by "is".
annotation.definitionFit: A passing is a death, and something passing lasts only a short while.

clue.text: Where one’s driven round the bend incessantly? (2,5,4)

definitions.text: Where one’s driven round the bend incessantly?

blocks.clueFragment: Where one’s driven round the bend
blocks.note: the surface offers being driven mad; read literally, it is a car being steered round a corner
not now and then but on each occasion, as a winding road has bend after bend

annotation.surface: Someone is being driven mad all the time.
annotation.walkthrough: "Driven round the bend" means driven crazy, but read literally it is a car taking a corner, which happens at every turn.
annotation.definitionFit: At every turn means constantly, on every occasion, which matches incessantly.

clue.text: Disorderly senior and artist get complaint (15)

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, with "and" joining them

annotation.surface: An unruly older man and a painter both come down with an illness.
annotation.walkthrough: "Get" looks like the verb joining the parts to the definition, but its letters are needed in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Gastroenteritis is a stomach and bowel illness, and complaint is a common word for an ailment.

clue.text: Key used to quickly get out of a window? (6)

definitions.text: Key used to quickly get out of a window?

blocks.clueFragment: Key used to quickly get out
blocks.note: the surface offers a door key; this is a key on a computer keyboard
not a pane of glass but a box on a screen, which that key closes

annotation.surface: A burglar or prisoner using a key to slip out through a window.
annotation.walkthrough: The window is on a computer screen, not in a wall, and the key is on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: The Escape key on a keyboard is often used to close or leave a window or dialog.

clue.text: Decline of Rome … ultimately that’s Gibbon’s focus (3)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the end of Rome is used
the focus of something is its centre, so take the middle of the word

blocks.note: the two middle letters of Gibbon

annotation.surface: The decline of Rome was Edward Gibbon's great subject.
annotation.walkthrough: Gibbon wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, so the surface is historically apt. "Decline" is also the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To ebb is to decline or fall away, as the tide does.

clue.text: Arms-running company unionist managed over time (7)

annotation.surface: A gun-running firm run by a Northern Irish unionist for some time.
annotation.walkthrough: "Arms" means a coat of arms, not weapons: courant is the heraldry term for an animal shown running. "Over" in a down clue puts RAN above T.
annotation.definitionFit: In heraldry an animal courant is depicted running, so it is running on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Sorry folk writer interviewed at front by shelters (9)

indicators.note: only what stands at the front of interviewed is used, its first letter

annotation.surface: An apologetic folk-song writer gives an interview at the front of some marquees.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sorry folk writer" reads as a songwriter, but the definition is "Sorry folk", people who repent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: penitent means sorry for wrongdoing, and as a noun it names a person who repents.

clue.text: Non-masculine ways of doing creative works (4)

indicators.note: the M for masculine is not there

blocks.note: modes are ways of doing things

annotation.surface: A remark about the less macho approaches to making art.
annotation.walkthrough: M is the dictionary abbreviation for masculine; drop it from MODES.
annotation.definitionFit: Odes are poems, a kind of creative work.

clue.text: A sober tune composed in coastal resort (10)

indicators.note: the letters are put together in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A sedate melody is written in a seaside town.
annotation.walkthrough: "Composed" suits the music in the surface; it also means calm, echoing "sober". EASTBOURNE is a seaside town in East Sussex, England.
annotation.definitionFit: Eastbourne is a resort on the south coast of England.

clue.text: One gulped before getting rid of black dog? (14)

definitions.text: One gulped before getting rid of black dog?

blocks.note: the surface suggests a nervous swallow; it is a pill being swallowed
not a pet but Churchill's name for his depression

annotation.surface: Someone nervously swallows before getting rid of a black dog.
annotation.walkthrough: "Black dog" was Churchill's name for his depression; the pill is swallowed to drive it off.
annotation.definitionFit: An antidepressant is a medicine taken to treat depression, the black dog.

clue.text: Awful cast sneer at system of Equity for presenters (6,5)

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad state, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: A terrible cast of actors mocks the actors' union's rules for TV hosts.
annotation.walkthrough: Equity is the actors' union in Britain, which fits "cast" and "presenters"; here equity is fairness, and presenters are people giving presents.
annotation.definitionFit: Secret Santa is a scheme where each person gives one present, so every giver is treated alike.

clue.text: Hammy sides of game served in lodge (6)

indicators.note: take the two edge letters
food served in a dish sits inside it, so GE goes inside the word for lodge

blocks.note: to lodge somewhere is to stay there
first and last letters of game

annotation.surface: Game in a hunting lodge is served with an exaggerated flourish.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hammy" and "game" point to a meal of meat; hammy here means overacted. "Lodge" is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Stagey acting is exaggerated and theatrical, just like hammy acting.

clue.text: Cope with Leith criminal? They will! (3,6)

definitions.text: Cope with Leith criminal? They will!

indicators.note: the letters are misbehaving, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Who can handle a lawbreaker from Leith? The cops can.
annotation.walkthrough: Leith is the port district of Edinburgh. The whole clue is also the definition: the police are who cope with criminals.
annotation.definitionFit: Dealing with criminals is the job of the police.

clue.text: Going away around fourth of March is dramatic (8)

indicators.note: the first word goes round the next piece
the fourth of a word is its fourth letter in order

annotation.surface: Leaving at the start of March makes a thrilling getaway.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fourth of March" looks like a date; it is the fourth letter of the word March.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dramatic finish and an exciting finish both grip the audience.

clue.text: Nut loaf just served with slice of toast (4,4)

indicators.note: take a small piece, the first letter

blocks.note: use your loaf means use your head
but means only, as in but a moment

annotation.surface: A nut roast is served with a piece of toast.
annotation.walkthrough: "Nut loaf" sounds like a vegetarian dish; nut is slang for hitting someone with your head, and "loaf" is rhyming slang for head (loaf of bread).
annotation.definitionFit: To nut someone is British slang for headbutting them.

clue.text: Perform first of dates with Stones and Fairground Attraction (7)

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to do a turn is to perform

annotation.surface: A band plays the opening gig of a tour alongside the Rolling Stones and Fairground Attraction.
annotation.walkthrough: Stones and Fairground Attraction look like bands (Fairground Attraction had a 1988 hit); dodgems are bumper cars at a funfair.
annotation.definitionFit: Dodgems, small electric bumper cars, are a classic fairground ride.

clue.text: In hearing, old partner scrutinizes tax (6)

indicators.note: the letters come from how the words are said

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner, and to eye something is to scrutinize it

annotation.surface: At a court hearing, a former spouse goes over the tax return.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hearing" suggests a court case, which fits the divorce and tax story; it signals the sound of the words.
annotation.definitionFit: Excise is a tax on goods such as alcohol and tobacco.

clue.text: Cold, injured and lucky to be alive? (7)

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone frozen and hurt is fortunate to have survived.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the phrase "a charmed life": someone who survives danger again and again seems protected by a charm.
annotation.definitionFit: To lead a charmed life is to escape harm by apparent luck.

clue.text: Low-grade salt in San Marino ready for refinement (8,6)

indicators.note: the letters are to be reworked into a better form

annotation.surface: Cheap salt from San Marino needs refining before it can be used.
annotation.walkthrough: Salt is an old word for a sailor, not table salt; an ordinary seaman is the lowest sailor rank in the Royal Navy.
annotation.definitionFit: Salt is an old word for sailor, and ordinary seaman is the lowest rating in the Royal Navy, hence low-grade.

clue.text: A horse rearing around one once more (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rearing up turns the word upside down
the reversed word goes round the next piece

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse

annotation.surface: A horse rears up over a rider yet again.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rearing" is what a horse does, which hides that it reverses NAG.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to do something again is to do it once more.

clue.text: Beastly type in a temper around about noon (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters are turned around into a new order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

annotation.surface: Someone nasty loses their temper around midday.
annotation.walkthrough: "Beastly type" suggests a nasty person; it means a type of beast, an animal. "About" places N close by, at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The pine marten is a small tree-dwelling animal of the weasel family.

clue.text: When rings start to smuggle dope (3)

indicators.note: the first word surrounds the next piece
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: as means when, as in as I left

annotation.surface: A drug ring gets going by smuggling narcotics.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dope" suggests drugs, which suits "rings" and "smuggle"; here a dope is a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a fool; dope in this sense has nothing to do with drugs.

clue.text: Guy ropes in English base (4)

indicators.note: the first word catches the next piece inside it

annotation.surface: Tent guy ropes at an English camp.
annotation.walkthrough: "Guy ropes" reads as tent lines; Guy is a man, and ropes in is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Base and mean both describe a low, contemptible act.

clue.text: Periods of abstinence broken by these at last? (6)

definitions.text: Periods of abstinence broken by these at last?

indicators.note: the next piece breaks into the first word
at last means at the end, so only the final letter of these is used

annotation.surface: Fasting ends when the banquets finally arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: feasts are what break fasts, and the E breaks FASTS too.
annotation.definitionFit: A feast is how a fast is broken, as with Eid after Ramadan.

clue.text: Upright reputation (8)

definitions.note: Upright is an adjective and reputation a noun; standing can be both

blocks.note: one's status or good name in others' eyes

annotation.surface: A good name for honesty, as in an upright reputation.
annotation.walkthrough: "Upright reputation" reads as one phrase about honesty; upright here is literal, standing up.
annotation.definitionFit: Standing means upright on one's feet, and also status or reputation.
